title: Sunny and the Banksia Pods
description: Little Sonny the quokka discovers the strange and wonderful banksia pods scattered across the forest floor. A curious, calm bedtime story for little ones. Part of Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
One afternoon, Sunny was exploring a part of the bush he didn't visit very often.

The trees here were tall and old, with rough grey bark and branches that spread wide and high. And on the ground, all around him, were the most interesting things Sunny had ever seen.

Banksia pods.

They were everywhere — big and small, old and new. Some were rough and woody like tiny carved faces. Some were split open, their seeds long gone, with little holes that looked almost like small surprised mouths.

Sunny picked one up carefully in his paws.

It was heavier than it looked. It had a strange, ancient feeling, like it had been waiting a very long time to be noticed.

Sunny turned it over and over, running his small fingers along the ridges. He found a perfect pod, still whole and smooth, like a tiny treasure.

He sat down right there on the quiet forest floor and arranged his collection in a row.

Big, medium, small. Old, middle, new. He didn't know exactly what he was doing. He just liked looking at them, feeling them, noticing how each one was different in its own particular way.

A honeyeater landed nearby, tipped its head at Sunny's collection, and flew away again.

Sunny smiled.

The afternoon light turned golden between the tall banksia trees. The air smelled of dry bark and eucalyptus and something warm and earthy.

Sunny stayed there until the light began to fade, looking at his pods, thinking his quiet thoughts.

Then he set them back down gently, one by one, and headed home along the winding path.

Goodnight, little Sunny. Goodnight, banksia pods. Goodnight, old and wonderful forest.
